item.aggregated_output:
How an agent should drive teapot

1. List the topics
   teapot guide

2. Every command with its effect
   teapot schema

3. The arguments, result and error shapes of one command
   teapot schema flows show --json

4. Add --json for the envelope {"<key>": ..., "advice": [...]} on stdout
   teapot flows list --json

5. Errors are {"error": {...}} on stderr with a `fix` command; the exit code says which kind
   teapot flows show nonexistent --json

6. Captured data is escaped in text output; --raw turns that off
   teapot flows show 412 --raw

7. Anything that changes state can be previewed
   teapot config set proxy.port 9090 --dry-run

8. Act on what a person selected in the TUI (@sel; name the TUI when several are attached)
   teapot clients list

9. @sel of one TUI: the reply states the flow ID it resolved to
   teapot flows show @sel --client tui-1

10. A TUI holds this open to be attached (it gives the client ID)
   teapot clients attach --json

11. And publishes its selection with
   teapot clients select tui-1 --flow 12

List captured flows

Usage: teapot flows list [OPTIONS] [FILTER]...

Arguments:
  [FILTER]...  Filter terms (`host:api.example.com status:5xx`); every term must
               match. No filter lists every flow. The grammar is in this command's
               help.

Options:
      --after <CURSOR>  Continue after this cursor, from the `next-page` advice of the call
                        before (same filter, sort and order).
      --count           Count the matching flows instead of listing them.
  -n, --limit <LIMIT>   Most rows, 1 to 1000. [default: 50]
      --order <ORDER>   `newest` (default) or `oldest` first. [default: newest] [possible values: newest, oldest]
      --sort <SORT>     What to order by: `id`, `time`, `size` or `status` (flows in flight last). [default: id] [possible values: id, time, size, status]
  -h, --help            Print help

Global options: --project, --format/--json, --fields, --no-header, --raw, --quiet and --no-color apply; the engine flags (--pass, --enforce, --lock-policy), --yes and --dry-run do not (see `teapot --help`).

Lists the project's flows, newest first, filtered by the filter language (plan 6.4). Pages are cut by a keyset cursor: the `next-page` advice gives the cursor and the command for the next page. Paging by ID (the default) visits every matching flow once even while flows are being captured. With `--sort time|size|status`, flows still in flight (live or intercepted) come last, by ID, in either order: paging lists no flow twice and every flow that did not end meanwhile once, but a flow that ends while you page moves to its final place and is missed if the pages already passed it. Filters on bodies and other terms the index cannot answer are checked flow by flow; that work is bounded per call, and when it stops early the reply says so (`scan-stopped`) with the command that continues. Text shows the columns of `--fields` (default: id method host path status size type time refused); --json has every field. With the engine running, the list first waits (at most one store batch) for what the engine has already captured, so a flow whose client has its answer is there; one still in flight shows as `state:live`. Read-only; works with no engine running.

Filter grammar: terms separated by a space must all match; `or`, `not` (or a leading `-`) and parentheses combine them; a bare word or "quoted phrase" searches the URL, headers and bodies; `field:value` tests one field; `field~/regex/i` is a regular expression (`i`: ignore case). Fields: host, status, method, path, url, scheme, port, type, size, req.size, res.size, time, header, req.header, res.header, body, req.body, res.body, is, has, state, noise, tag, session, in. `host:example.com` includes its subdomains. `path:/admin` is a prefix on a segment boundary (/admin, /admin/x; not /administrator) and `path:/api/*` is a glob over the whole path. `status:` is the HTTP status (`404`, `5xx`, `>=400`), never the flow's state: use `state:` (live, intercepted, complete, error, passthrough, malformed, interrupted). `is:` takes intercepted, replay, websocket, error, refused, noise, tls, challenge (a bot-protection challenge, tagged `challenge`); `has:` takes finding, response, body, cookie. `tag:` takes a tag name or glob: the browser's own service calls that teapot refused carry `tag:browser-own`; every refused flow, with its code in the `refused` field, matches `is:refused`. Sizes take kb/mb, times take ms/s (`size:>1mb time:>2s`).

Noise: every flow has a noise class, given when it was captured: `static` (images, fonts, stylesheets and media, by content type or file extension; a script is never static), `telemetry` (analytics and ad beacons), `browser` (the browser's own updates, Safe Browsing, connectivity and captive-portal checks), or `none`. `noise:none`, `noise:static`, `noise:telemetry`, `noise:browser` and `noise:any` (every class but `none`, the same as `is:noise`) filter on it; `--fields noise` shows it. This command never hides noise: every flow is listed, and when some of the rows shown are noise an advice line (`noise-shown`) gives how many and the command that leaves them out. (The TUI hides noise by default.) Traffic to a host in scope is never noise, except static assets (a stylesheet of the target is `static`). The bundled list can be extended and overridden in `config.toml` (`[noise] extra`, `never`; read when the engine starts). A flow captured before noise classes existed (project schema 3) has no class until the engine first starts over the project: it classifies each such flow once, with the `[noise]` and scope of that start, and until then the flow reads as `none`. Stored classes are not recomputed when the config or scope changes later.

Examples:
  # Server errors from one API
  teapot flows list host:api.example.com status:5xx --limit 2
  412  POST  api.example.com  /v1/orders       500  1.2kb  json  83ms  -
  398  GET   api.example.com  /v1/users/17     502  0      -     30s   -
  Next: teapot flows show 412

  # The slowest flows
  teapot flows list --sort time

  # Flows teapot refused to send
  teapot flows list is:refused

  # The browser's own refused calls
  teapot flows list tag:browser-own

  # Flows still in flight
  teapot flows list state:live

  # The first complete flow (skips error flows)
  teapot flows list state:complete --order oldest --limit 1

  # How many flows logged in
  teapot flows list path:/login --count

  # Pick the columns
  teapot flows list --fields id,status,path,time_ms

Agent workflow:
  # Find the flows
  teapot flows list status:5xx --json
  {"flows":[{"id":412,"method":"POST","host":"api.example.com","path":"/v1/orders","status":500,...}],"advice":[{"level":"info","type":"next-page","message":"after 412","command":"teapot flows list status:5xx --after 412"},...]}

  # Look at one
  teapot flows show 412 --json

  # Next page
  teapot flows list status:5xx --after 412 --json

Read-only; runs without an engine when none is running.
Exit codes: 0 ok, 1 usage error, 2 system error, 3 gate failed, 4 refused.

  /                          this table, as text
  /hello                     200, short text body with Content-Length
  /echo                      what the origin received: method, target, headers in order, body length and SHA-256
  /echo/json                 what the origin received as JSON: method, target, version, headers in order, body, length, SHA-256
  /echo/raw                  the request head byte for byte, then the body
  /v1/orders                 POST a JSON order: 200 summary; 500 with a stack-trace-like body for a negative items[].qty; 400 for a non-order
  /status                    an empty response with the given status [code=200]
  /expect                    Expect: 100-continue handling, then reports the body length [mode=continue|silent|reject]
  /chunked                   chunked body, one write per chunk [chunks=3 size=16 delay_ms=0]
  /chunked/odd               legal but odd chunking: leading zeros, upper-case hex, extensions, trailers

  /sse                       text/event-stream that stays open, one event per interval [count=0 interval_ms=1000 framing=chunked|close]

item.text:
**Cross-user access remains unverified.** On `http://127.0.0.1:43865`, Alice’s and Bob’s sessions each returned the correct account identity. Both inboxes were empty, so the inbox comparison provides no evidence about access to another user’s messages.

| Request | Alice’s session | Bob’s session |
|---|---|---|
| `GET /app/api/me` | `200` · `{"id":2,"role":"user","user":"alice"}` | `200` · `{"id":3,"role":"user","user":"bob"}` |
| `GET /app/messages` | `200` · “Signed in as alice” · “You have no new messages.” | `200` · “Signed in as bob” · “You have no new messages.” |

`GET /app/account` returned `200` for all three demo accounts. Only the admin account saw a link to `/app/admin`. That establishes role-specific navigation. Server-side enforcement on the admin route and cross-user read or write access to individual records remain unverified.
